value.signature: fn cmp (& self , other : & Value) -> Ordering

exception.justification: Justified: Structural value traits inherit the labelled canonical coding and theory operation that consumes the value; recording them again would duplicate full payloads during hashing, comparison, cloning or teardown.

review.body: { let mut work : Vec < (& Value , & Value) > = vec ! [(self , other)] ; while let Some ((a , b)) = work . pop () { match a . canonical_head () . cmp (& b . canonical_head ()) { Ordering :: Equal => { } unequal => return unequal , } match (a , b) { (Value :: Bytes (x) , Value :: Bytes (y)) => match x . as_slice () . cmp (y . as_slice ()) { Ordering :: Equal => { } unequal => return unequal , } , (Value :: Text (x) , Value :: Text (y)) => match x . as_str () . cmp (y . as_str ()) { Ordering :: Equal => { } unequal => return unequal , } , (Value :: Array (x) , Value :: Array (y)) => { work . extend (x . as_slice () . iter () . zip (y . as_slice ()) . rev ()) ; } (Value :: Map (x) , Value :: Map (y)) => { for ((xk , xv) , (yk , yv)) in x . 0 . iter () . zip (y . 0 . iter ()) . rev () { work . push ((xv , yv)) ; work . push ((xk , yk)) ; } } (Value :: Tag (x) , Value :: Tag (y)) => work . push ((x . item () , y . item ())) , _ => { } } } Ordering :: Equal }
